note: D -- rules with at least one mutation observed provoking them. May rise, never fall. The entries are in enforce/discrimination.py and are meant to be read; the count alone says nothing about whether they are good.
why: v3.1 Phase 2: the auto mutation kind. Twenty-seven binding rules are decided by a configured tool alone and no mutation kind could reach them, so D was structurally incapable of covering them. Thirteen now do: three import contracts, six ruff codes (five of them PROTECTED), two mypy codes. Writing them found that four of the eight auto:import-linter rules were named by no contract at all.
